'''Władysław Zygmunt Ślebodziński''' ({{IPA|pl|vwaˈdɨswaf ɕlɛbɔˈd͡ʑij̃skʲi}}; 6 February 1884 – 3 January 1972) was a Polish [[mathematician]], a former [[Auschwitz concentration camp]] prisoner, a professor at the [[Wrocław University of Technology]] and a member of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]]. 

In 1961–1963, he served as president of the [[Polish Mathematical Society]]. He was a co-founder and a leading representative of the Wroclaw School of Mathematics. He is noted for introducing an operator in [[differential geometry]] later named the [[Lie derivative]].

== Life and career ==
===Early life and education===
[[File:Władysław in 1895.JPG|thumb|left|180px|Ślebodziński in 1895]]
Władysław Ślebodziński was born on 6 February 1884 in [[Pysznica]],<ref name="Kopia">{{cite book | last= Kopia | first= Henryk | title= Spis nauczycieli szkół średnich w Galicyi oraz polskiego gimnazyum w Cieszynie |trans-title=List of Teachers of Secondary Schools in Galicia and of the Polish Gymnasium in Cieszyn | publisher= Towarzystwo Nauczycieli Szkół Wyższych | location   = Lviv | year= 1909 | page= 104 | language= pl}}</ref> then part of the [[Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria]], as the son of Ignacy and Anna ({{nee|Gorylska}}).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dziennikustaw.gov.pl/mp/1954/s/112/1589 |language=pl |title=Uchwała Rady Państwa z dnia 28 września 1954 r. o nadaniu odznaczeń państwowych |trans-title=“Resolution of the Council of State of 28 September 1954 on the awarding of state decorations |website=dziennikustaw.gov.pl |access-date=29 August 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sejm-wielki.pl/b/sw.661295 |language=pl |title=Władysław Zygmunt Ślebodziński |work=sejm-wielki.pl |access-date=29 August 2026}}</ref> In 1903–1908, he studied mathematics and physics at the [[Jagiellonian University]] in [[Kraków]].<ref name="HMatuszczyk">{{cite journal
| last       = Langner-Matuszczykowa
| first      = Hanna
| author-link = 
| title      = Władysław Ślebodziński -- matematyk, więzień KL Auschwitz Nr 29053.
| journal    = Śląska Republika Uczonych - Schlesische Gelehrtenrepublik - Slezzka vedecka obec
| publisher = Neiss Verlag (Dresden); Oficyna Wydawnicza ATUT - Wrocławskie Wydawnictwo Oświatowe (Wrocław)
| volume     = VII
| issue      = 2016
| pages      = 399–425
| issn = 1733-2699
}}</ref>  

In 1908, he bacame a teacher of mathematics and worked at [[gymnasium (school)|gymnasiums]] in [[Sanok]] and [[Tarnobrzeg]]. In 1912, Ślebodziński transferred to Kraków where he held a teaching position at the Imperial-Royal Real School.<ref name="MacTut"/> In 1913–1914, he pursued further studies at the [[University of Göttingen]]<ref name="PohlKost">{{cite web|url=https://weny.pwr.edu.pl/d/DGBUKOTtQKxVvA0x0ShNuClBQSXt8X0FABWdbExYbWGFBRAg9RgNtcXccVjU3ClVBDkNGfXteWVUU/wladyslaw-slebodzinski.pdf |language=pl |title=Władysław Ślebodziński 1884 – 1972 |work=Wrocław University of Technology |author=Zbigniew Pohl, Andrzej Kostowski |access-date=29 August 2026}}</ref> attending lectures  by [[Constantin Carathéodory]], [[Edmund Landau]] and [[David Hilbert]].<ref name="MacTut"/> 

===Career beginnings===
During [[World War I]], Ślebodziński served only six months in the [[Austro-Hungarian Army|Austrian Army]] before being transferred back to Kraków at the Imperial-Royal Real School due to his essential role in education. In this period, Ślebodziński became acquainted with such prominent mathematicians as [[Hugo Steinhaus]], [[Stefan Banach]], and  [[Włodzimierz Stożek]].<ref name="MacTut"/>

In the 1920s, Ślebodziński lectured in mathematics at the Faculty of Pharmacy of the [[University of Poznań]]. He simultaneously taught mathematics at the State School of Machine Construction ([[Polish language|Polish]]: ''Państwowa Szkoła Budowy Maszyn'').<ref>{{cite book | last= Zagórowski | first= Zygmunt | title= Spis nauczycieli szkół wyższych, średnich, zawodowych, seminarjów nauczycielskich oraz wykaz zakładów naukowych i władz szkolnych |trans-title=List of Teachers of Higher, Secondary, Vocational, and Teacher‑Training Schools, together with a Register of Scientific Institutions and Educational Authorities | publisher= Książnica Polska | location= Lwów/Warsaw | year= 1924 | page= 414 | language= pl}}</ref>  He was also active in the Association of Teachers of Secondary and Higher Schools (TNSW) serving as chairman of the Poznań branch of the organization in 1924.<ref>{{cite book | last= Zagórowski | first= Zygmunt | title= Spis nauczycieli szkół wyższych, średnich, zawodowych, seminarjów nauczycielskich oraz wykaz zakładów naukowych i władz szkolnych |trans-title=List of Teachers of Higher, Secondary, Vocational, and Teacher‑Training Schools, together with a Register of Scientific Institutions and Educational Authorities | publisher= Książnica Polska | location= Lwów/Warsaw | year= 1924 | page= 439, 422 | language= pl}}</ref>

In 1927, Ślebodziński participated in the First Polish Mathematical Congress in [[Lwów]], having been appointed chairman of the Geometry Section. In 1928, Ślebodziński earned his [[doctorate]] at the [[University of Warsaw]] based on his thesis '' O pewnej klasie powierzchni Riemanna'' (On a Certain Class of Riemann Surfaces) written under the supervision of [[Kazimierz Żorawski]].<ref name="MathGen">{{cite web|url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=157629 |title=Władysław Ślebodziński |work=Mathematics Genealogy Project |access-date=29 August 2026}}</ref> In 1934, he obtained his [[habilitation]] and started work as a [[docent]] at the University of Warsaw.<ref name="MacTut"/>
[[File:8731viki Politechnika Wrocławska ul. Wybrzeże Wyspiańskiego. Foto Barbara Maliszewska.jpg|thumb|270px|Ślebodziński was affiliated with the [[Wrocław University of Technology]] for much of his career]]

===World War II===
During the [[World War II]], he was forced to relocate from [[Poznań]] to [[Bochnia]] in southern Poland.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sztafeta.pl/artykuly/wspoltworca-wroclawskiej-szkoly-matematycznej-urodzil-sie-w-pysznicy |language=pl |title=Współtwórca wrocławskiej szkoły matematycznej urodził się w Pysznicy |trans-title=The Co-founder of the Wrocław School of Mathematics Was Born in Pysznica |author=Lilla Witkowska |website=sztafeta.pl |access-date=29 August 2026}}</ref> He gave [[Education in Poland during World War II|underground lectures]], leading to his imprisonment by [[Nazi Germany]]. He survived three German concentration camps: [[Auschwitz]] (1942–1945), where he gave underground university-level lectures as prisoner no. 79053 and survived the [[Death marches during the Holocaust|"Death March"]] to [[Wodzisław Śląski]] after the camp had been evacuated before the advancement of the Soviet troops in 1945;<ref name="MacTut"/> [[Gross-Rosen]]; and [[Mittelbau-Dora concentration camp|Nordhausen]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Władysław Ślebodziński |url=https://www.morebooks.de/store/gb/book/w%C5%82adys%C5%82aw-%C5%9Alebodzi%C5%84ski/isbn/978-613-8-67272-2}}</ref> 

===Postwar career===
In 1945, he became a joint professor at [[Wrocław University]] and at the [[Wrocław University of Technology]], and from 1951 he was a professor at the [[Wrocław University of Technology]]. From 1949 until 1960, he was a Professor of the [[Institute of Mathematics of the Polish Academy of Sciences|Institute of Mathematics]] of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]].

In 1950, he was one of the co-founders of the journal ''Colloquim Mathematicum'' alongside [[Edward Marczewski]], [[Bronisław Knaster]] and [[Hugo Steinhaus]].<ref name="MacTut">{{cite web|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Slebodzinski/ |title=Władysław Ślebodziński |work=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive]] | author=J.J. O'Connor, E.F. Robertson |access-date=29 August 2026}}</ref> He is also considered one of the founders of the Wrocław School of Mathematics.<ref name="PohlKost"></ref> The relations between the four mathematicians are described by {{ill|Roman Duda|pl}} and {{ill|Aleksander Weron|pl}} as follows:<ref>{{cite journal | last1= Duda | first1= Roman | last2= Weron | first2= Aleksander | title= Wrocławska szkoła matematyczna |trans-title=The Wrocław School of Mathematics | journal= Wiadomości Matematyczne | volume= XLII | year= 2006 | page= 75 | language= pl}}</ref>

<blockquote>They were united by a pioneering zeal and a firm conviction that Wrocław was, and would remain, Polish, as well as by their determination to settle there permanently. As mathematicians, they possessed a substantial body of work recognized internationally, which gave them considerable and natural academic authority; they knew their own worth and held one another in high esteem. All four settled in [the district of] Biskupin (...), which had survived the devastation of [[Siege of Breslau|the siege]], a circumstance that fostered close and friendly relations among them.</blockquote>

Between 1961–1963, he served as president of the [[Polish Mathematical Society]].<ref name="MacTut"/> His notable students included [[Witold Roter]], {{ill|Ryszard Deszcz|pl|Ryszard Deszcz}}, {{ill|Stefan Drobot|pl|Stefan Drobot}}, {{ill|Abraham Goetz|pl|Abraham Goetz}}, and {{ill|Tadeusz Huskowski|pl|Tadeusz Huskowski}}.<ref name="MathGen"></ref>

He died on 3 January 1972, in [[Wrocław]], and is buried in the Wrocław Cemetery located in Sępolno.<ref name=WSgrave>{{cite web|title=''Grave record for Władysław Ślebodziński (6 Feb 1884 - 3 Jan 1972), BillionGraves Record 16763151 Wrocław, wrocławski, dolnośląskie, Poland''|url=https://billiongraves.com/grave/W%C5%82adys%C5%82aw-%C5%9Alebodzi%C5%84ski/16763151|accessdate=2021-02-24}}</ref>

===Personal life===
In 1908, he married Anna Gisella {{nee|Zarnecka}} (1879-1970) in St. Nicholas Church in Kraków. They had two children: son Lesław, a chemistry teacher, and daughter Zofia Krystyna, a mathematics teacher and a graduate of the [[University of Poznań]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.matematyka.wroc.pl/matematykawsztuce/matematyczne-zaduszki |language=pl |title=Matematyczne zaduszki |trans-title=Mathematical All Souls' Day |author=Małgorzata Mikołajczyk |website=matematyka.wroc.pl |access-date=29 August 2026}}</ref><ref name="MacTut"/>

==Awards, decorations, and honors==
*1958: Commander's Cross of the [[Order of Polonia Restituta]]<ref name="MacTut"/>
*1955: {{ill|Polish State Award badge|lt=Polish State Award|pl|Odznaka Nagrody Państwowej}} (team award of 2nd degree) for his contributions in differential geometry<ref>"Nagrody państwowe za osiągnięcia w dziedzinie nauki...", In: ''[[Życie Warszawy]]'', [https://mbc.cyfrowemazowsze.pl/Content/63005/PDF/00067830%20-%20%C5%BBycie%20Warszawy%201955%20nr%20173%20-%20P10019.pdf year XII, No. 173 (3656), p. 5, July 22, 1955]</ref>
*1954: [[Cross of Merit (Poland)|Polish Golden Cross of Merit]], for his scientific achievements<ref>[https://sip.lex.pl/akty-prawne/mp-monitor-polski/uchwala-rady-panstwa-z-dnia-28-wrzesnia-1954-r-nr-0-811-16808253 Uchwała rady państwa z dnia 28 września 1954 r. nr 0/811], ''[[Monitor Polski]]'', November 30, 1954</ref><ref name="Kopia"></ref>
*1918: [[1908 Jubilee Cross]] ([[Austria-Hungary]]),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://alex.onb.ac.at/cgi-content/alex?aid=shb&datum=1918&size=45&page=1403& |language=de |title=Hof- und Staatshandbuch der Österreichisch-Ungarischen Monarchie für das Jahr 1918 |work=Österreichische Nationalbibliothek |access-date=29 August 2026}}</ref>

He accepted [[honorary doctorate]]s from the [[Wrocław University of Technology]] (1965), [[Poznań University of Technology]] (1967),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304122937/http://www3.put.poznan.pl/jubileusz/honoriscausa |language=pl |title=Doktorzy honoris causa Politechniki Poznańskiej |trans-title=Honorary Doctorates of the Poznań University of Technology |work=Poznań University of Technology |access-date=29 August 2026}}</ref> and the [[University of Wrocław]] (1970).<ref>{{cite book | last= Cetwiński | first= Marek | title= Historia Wrocławia w datach |trans-title=History of Wrocław In Dates | editor= Gelles, Romuald | publisher= TMW Wratislawia | location= Wrocław | year= 1996 | page= 187 | language= pl}}</ref> He also became an honorary member of the Polish Mathematical Society.

==Contributions==
In his early career Ślebodziński was interested in [[Galois theory]];<ref name="MacTut"/> however, he later focused primarily on [[differential geometry]] and made his most important contributions in that area. In 1931,<ref>Ślebodziński W. (1931), ''Sur les équations de Hamilton'', Bull. Acad. Roy. d. Belg. 17 (5) pp. 864-870</ref> he introduced a new differential operator known as the [[Lie derivative]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/4F3305F81F1EA9AFC6C4C07C9935C468/S0013091500025013a.pdf/the-definition-of-lie-derivative.pdf |title=The Definition of Lie Derivative |work=Cambridge University Press |author=T.J. Willmore |date=2 May 1959 |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref> in his work titled ''Sur les équations canoniques de Hamilton''. According to [[Jan Arnoldus Schouten|J.A. Schouten]],<ref>Schouten J.A.  (1954), ''Ricci-Calculus'', Springer-Verlag, page 105</ref> it was [[David van Dantzig]] who named the operation "Lie derivative" (after [[Sophus Lie]])<ref>{{cite book |first=A. |last=Trautman |author-link=Andrzej Trautman |year=2008 |chapter=Remarks on the history of the notion of Lie differentiation |title=Variations, Geometry and Physics: In honour of Demeter Krupka's sixty-fifth birthday |editor1-first=O. |editor1-last=Krupková |editor2-first=D. J. |editor2-last=Saunders |location=New York |publisher=Nova Science |isbn=978-1-60456-920-9 |pages=297–302 }}</ref> for the first time in a two-part paper published in 1932 acknowledging it was Ślebodziński who had introduced it.<ref>Dantzig D. van (1932) ''Zur allgemeinen projektiven Differentialgeometrie I, II.'', Proc. Kon. Akad. Amsterdam 35 pp. 524-534; pp. 535-542</ref> 

The Lie derivative evaluates the change of a [[tensor field]] eg. scalar functions, [[vector field]]s and [[one-form]]s, along the [[flow (mathematics)|flow]] defined by another vector field. It played a significant role in the rapid advancement of several branches of differential geometry serving as a crucial and highly effective tool in the study of [[automorphism group]]s and finding broad, meaningful applications throughout [[geometry]].<ref name="MacTut"/>
